regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.claim: “Try Sucraid®” | “Do you have patients suffering with unresolved IBS-like symptoms, including gas, bloating, diarrhea, and/or nausea?” | “Could it be CSID?” | “Learn more about the only FDA-approved enzyme replacement therapy for the treatment of CSID...”
cases.context: Full indication ('treatment of sucrase deficiency, which is part of CSID') only at bottom with ISI in small plain font after eye-catching graphics.
cases.rationale: Implies use for IBS and for all contributing factors of CSID; indication is limited to sucrase deficiency.
cases.check: Does the piece invite use in a broader population (e.g., symptom-based, related conditions) than the labeled indication?

cases.claim: Emails omit WARNINGS: Severe Hypersensitivity Reactions; PRECAUTIONS: Increased Blood Glucose Concentration in Patients with Diabetes Mellitus; Dietary Starch Restriction (“Sucraid does not replace isomaltase...”).
cases.rationale: Omits material risk information from the PI.
cases.check: Rule: verify each Warning and Precaution heading from the PI is represented in the piece's safety information.

cases.cat: Minimization of risk (order of risk presentation)
cases.claim: Risk information pertaining to the ADVERSE REACTIONS section of the PI is presented prior to the risk information pertaining to the PRECAUTION section of the PI (i.e., Increased Blood Glucose Concentrations in Patients with Diabetes Mellitus).
cases.rationale: Risk not disclosed in order of severity, framing serious risks as less serious.
cases.check: Rule: risk statements must follow label severity order (Boxed Warning > Contraindications > W&P > Adverse Reactions).
